name: Remove the Collect Every Applicant command, its button and its branch of the walk
request: Remove the Collect Every Applicant command, its button and its branch of the walk
checks: npm run check passed: typecheck, build, 432 tests, validate
result: Removed the Collect Every Applicant command: its button and handler in the popup and on the Applicants page, and the per-row branch of the walk it was the only caller of. It was never a second walk - options.listOnly chose between two per-row bodies inside one loop, and the row loop, identity ledger, page roster, growApplicantList, pagination, conclusive-stop rule, collected index, arrival guard, auto-run and reload-resume were all already shared; by 3.7.11 the two bodies had converged too, so what went is one branch and one button, not a capability. extractApplicant is now the surface's one per-row path, called both by the walk and by PV_APPLICANT_EXTRACT. The already-collected check deleted with the branch was a duplicate of the bulk retirement above it. options.listOnly is still accepted and no longer read, so a run armed by the previous build resumes rather than falling into a branch that is gone. recollect moved to Collect Applicant List rather than being deleted - it is a property of a run, not of one button, and unchecked it sends false, which is the walk's own default. Kept and asserted by a new test: Collect This Applicant, Collect Applicant List, extractApplicant (exactly one), sweepCurrentPage and the roster, clickApplicantPager, isConclusiveListStop, selectApplicantRow, the PERMANENT resume chain, the contact disclosure, continueInterruptedRun, pumpAutoRun and the seven-click budget. background.ts, applicants-core.js, messages.ts, the databases, the manifest, content.js and connections.js are untouched. Five assertions were repointed at collectVisibleApplicant, where the clauses they lock now live - including the PERMANENT one-click-per-applicant test, which gained a count of the row clicks on that path and was not weakened.
